newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Megawati to answer summons - lawyer.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Megawati to answer summons - lawyer.

text.p: Megawati Sukarnoputri, ousted leader of the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI), will answer a police summons as a witness in a probe into an alleged illegal meeting at her house, a lawyer said on Wednesday.
"She will appear at the South Jakarta police station tomorrow. I have learnt that some of her supporters will also be there," Ahmad Dilapanga, one of Megawati's lawyers, told Reuters by telephone.

The function was held at Megawati's residence in South Jakarta on January 10 to celebrate the PDI's 24th anniversary. It was attended by hundreds of supporters who heard her deliver a speech critical of the government.
Megawati's husband, legislator Taufik Kiemas, was questioned as a witness by police at the South Jakarta station on Tuesday in connection with the investigation.
Megawati, who is also a member of parliament, failed to appear for questioning last week, citing faults in the summons.

Dilapanga said Megawati's summons still lacked the necessary presidential approval required before police could question a member of parliament. Police had only produced a letter from State Secretary Murdiono.
Megawati was ousted as PDI leader at a government-backed congress last June that replaced her with deputy speaker of parliament Surjadi.
Dilapanga said police had summoned Megawati and her husband as witnesses in an "illegal political meeting", but added that police had not so far named any suspects.
"Police have said they have not named any suspects because they are still conducting further investigation," he said.

Last year, police questioned Megawati as a witness in connection with the July 27 riots in Jakarta that followed a police-backed raid on PDI headquarters by Surjadi's supporters. No charges were filed against her.
At least five people died in the riots, the worst in the capital in more than two decades.
